column1: # One row per item of SKILL.md §Credential-hygiene checklist (16 items: E1-E8
# under "Evidence production:", H1-H8 under "Handler operation:"). Columns:
#   id <TAB> class <TAB> lead <TAB> check <TAB> expect_exit <TAB> expect_last
#   class runnable   check = command run with cwd = repo root, timeout 240 s;
#                    expect_exit = N or `A|B`; expect_last = ERE matched against
#                    the last non-blank stdout line; reason = `-`
#                    operator-scope); note = why no command shape exists
#   lead             ERE matched against the item text; the mapping must be a
#   note             what the row verifies (runnable) or why it cannot be
#                    mechanised and what would mechanise it (by-hand)
# Ground rules for a check string: metadata only. No row may read
# $CONFIG_DIR/op.env bytes, resolve a reference, exec `op`, or start/stop the
# handler; the gate refuses such a check (POLICY, exit 2). A check must print a
# verdict line and nothing secret — the gate echoes a failing row's output for
# diagnosis, so a row that prints a value would leak it into the run log.

column8: the item's duty is to run the declaration gate then the drift gate before citing a path; `&&` asserts both exits, the pinned last line is drift's verdict with the pin counts the item's own text states (15 files / 20 pins) — a count change is a reviewed re-pin event, not a pass

column7: manual-change: --pin runs once after an intentional host edit, and which REPIN/MOVED lines are acceptable is an authoring call
column8: the drift gate itself is row E1; the acceptance decision cannot be mechanised until re-pinning is itself a reviewed artifact

column3: Quote command output only when it is metadata-only
column7: authoring-duty: deciding that a quoted block is metadata-only is a writing judgement; no regex cleanly separates a metadata block from pasted output
column8: what would mechanise it: a declared allow-list of quotable command shapes, which would need the same authoring call one level up

column4: raw=$(grep -RInE --exclude-dir=.git 'op://[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]+' . | wc -l | tr -d ' '); ex=$(grep -RInE --exclude-dir=.git 'op://[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]+' . | grep -vE 'op://(vault|FakeVault|wal)/' | wc -l | tr -d ' '); printf 'REF_PATH_SCAN: hits=%s excluded=%s raw=%s\n' "$ex" "$((raw - ex))" "$raw"; test "$ex" -eq 0 && test "$raw" -eq 5
column8: scans **every non-`.git` file in the repo, any extension** (a lane's counterexample: an untracked `.json` carrying a reference literal passed an extension-filtered scan), and reports both the raw count and how many the allowlist removed, so the allowlist can never do its work silently. The allowlist is three declared placeholder/fixture vault names (`vault` — the documented example shape at three lines — plus the FakeVault and `wal` fixtures inside surface-census.sh and transcript-scan.sh); a live-looking path under any other vault name still hits, and both counts are pinned so removing an example line is a reviewed re-pin, not a pass. Counts only: printing the matched line would be the leak this item forbids

column6: ^OP_REF_PROBE: CLEAN \(checks=[0-9]+ oprun=[0-9]+ refs=[0-9]+ divergent=[0-9]+ edge=[0-9]+ sig=[0-9]+\)$

Bound, named rather than hidden: that gate is the ONE row here that execs `op run`, over generated plain-value fixtures, and its own POLICY guard refuses any op-side ref token before exec (exit 2), so no reference is resolved; it needs `op` on PATH and exits 2 (SETUP) otherwise — a competing reading classifies this row by-hand, which would make the split 8/8, exactly the floor

column4: c=$(grep -c '^[[:space:]]*flock 9' "$HOME/.local/bin/the-janitor" || true); e=$(grep -c '^[[:space:]]*exec 9>"\$LOCK_FILE"' "$HOME/.local/bin/the-janitor" || true); k=$(grep -c '^LOCK_FILE=' "$HOME/.local/bin/the-janitor" || true); m=$(stat -c '%a' "$HOME/.local/state/the-janitor/client.lock" 2>/dev/null || echo absent); printf 'CLIENT_LOCK: flock=%s exec=%s declared=%s mode=%s\n' "$c" "$e" "$k" "$m"; test "$c" -ge 2 && test "$e" -ge 2 && test "$k" = 1 && { test "$m" = 600 || test "$m" = absent; }
column8: the serialization premise behind the item: the flock sites, the `exec 9>` that opens the lock file, and the LOCK_FILE declaration in the CLI, plus the lock file's mode when it exists. Both code patterns are line-anchored (`^[[:space:]]*`), so a comment merely mentioning flock or exec does not satisfy the row (a lane's executed counterexample); the queue-instead-of-race half is the operator's behaviour, and the flock does not cover direct HTTP callers

column7: runtime-behavior: needs a stop then a next-request cycle against a live handler; start/stop is operator scope and deliberately outside this gate
column8: what would mechanise it: an operator-present --deep probe class, the same shape surface-census.sh already uses for its three real-world-effect probes

column6: ^(TRANSCRIPT_SCAN: HITS=2 \(cells=[0-9]+ patterns=[0-9]+\+[0-9]+ warns=[0-9]+ schema-absent=[0-9]+\) db=.*|transcript-scan: db not found: .*)$
column8: HITS=2 is the declared 2026-09-28 baseline and exit 1 is BY DESIGN (WARN/HIT cells are expected), so the pinned line is the teeth: a changed hit count is ITEM-LASTLINE, never a pass — re-pin only after reading the HIT lines. The second accepted state is the one the item above it prescribes: after `stop` + `rm -rf xdg-data` the DB is legitimately gone (surface-census classes `opencode.db*` runtime/absent), where the gate exits 2 with `db not found`; a THIRD state (any other exit-2 cause) still fails the row

column4: pw=$(grep -h -c OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD "$HOME/.local/bin/the-janitor" "$HOME/.config/the-janitor/client.py" | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}'); L=$(ss -ltnH 2>/dev/null | awk '$4 ~ /:40961$/ {n++} END{print n+0}'); NL=$(ss -ltnH 2>/dev/null | awk '$4 ~ /:40961$/ && $4 !~ /^127\.0\.0\.1:/ {n++} END{print n+0}'); E=$(ss -tnH state established 2>/dev/null | awk '$4 ~ /:40961$/ || $5 ~ /:40961$/ {n++} END{print n+0}'); printf 'CONTROL_PLANE: password_refs=%s listeners=%s non_loopback=%s established=%s\n' "$pw" "$L" "$NL" "$E"; test "$pw" -eq 0 && test "$E" -eq 0 && test "$NL" -eq 0
column8: the containment premise: neither the CLI nor the client sets OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD, no established socket points at 40961, and no listener on 40961 is bound off loopback. A loopback listener is legitimate while the handler runs, so the count is reported and only its non-loopback subset is asserted (a wildcard bind would expose the unauthenticated API; proven on scratch ports by a lane)
